content.title: Treasury Yields Mostly Rise as Markets Await Fed Decision
content.summary: U.S. Treasury yields were mostly rising in early trade as markets priced in unchanged interest rates at the Federal Reserve's rate decision on Wednesday. After cutting its key policy rate by 75 basis points in 2025, the Fed is expected to start 2026 with a pause, at least in the conventional component of its monetary policy, Natixis IM Solutions' Mabrouk Chetouane said in a note.

content.title: Investors Favor U.S. Treasuries Despite Unpredictable Politics
content.summary: U.S. Treasury yields have been fairly stable, even as the political environment in the U.S. is unpredictable, analysts at the Investment Institute by UniCredit said in a note.  Low volatility in U.S. Treasury yields indicates investors still favor the bonds, the analysts said.  Markets expect the U.S. Federal Reserve to cut interest rates further, which is likely to boost Treasuries' performance, they said.

content.title: Treasury Yields Fall as U.S. Shutdown Fears Grow, Fed Decision Looms
content.summary: Yields on Treasuries fell as investors continued to seek safe-haven assets as the risk of another U.S. government shutdown grows and investors await a Federal Reserve decision on Wednesday. Gold has broken above the $5,000-an-ounce barrier as Senate Democrats resist supporting a funding bill for the Department of Homeland Security after another fatal shooting in Minneapolis, risking a shutdown.
